Two documents on disk and both read: doc 75253 is a 6-page covering report whose figures all sit in doc 75254, the 32-page appendix dated February 2026. Every treasury figure below is quoted from the appendix. Scottish authority — statutory finance officer is a Section 95 Officer, and the paper's §5.6 is headed accordingly. Treasury advisor is MUFG Corporate Markets (appendix §1.6, formerly Link Group). The strategy is dated against MUFG's 22 December 2025 interest-rate view (appendix §5.2 page 20; header typo prints '22.12.26' but narrative and table page 13 both name the view as 22 December 2025).

facts.value: Total CFR £441.110m at 31 March 2025 actual; £436.860m projected 31 March 2026; rising to £468.733m (2026/27), £527.127m (2027/28), £557.802m (2028/29). CFR excluding OLTL: £298.014m (2024/25 actual) rising to £421.590m (2028/29). OLTL runs off gently from £143.096m to £136.212m over the same window.

£220.116m at 31 March 2025 (PWLB £191.693m; LA £20.000m; Market £7.085m; Temporary £1.338m). £229.363m at 27 February 2026 (PWLB £205.988m; LA £15.000m; Market £7.051m; Temporary £1.324m). Forward projections: Actual Gross Debt (incl OLTL) £380.611m (25/26), £429.524m (26/27), £499.662m (27/28), £534.925m (28/29).
facts.note: The two rows tie: 191.693+20.000+7.085+1.338 = 220.116; 205.988+15.000+7.051+1.324 = 229.363. All current borrowing is at a fixed interest rate (§4.20).

facts.value: £15.726m at 31 March 2025, all with Banks/Building Societies. £10.027m at 27 February 2026. §4.18: no significant cash balances anticipated over the upcoming period beyond day-to-day cash management.

facts.value: £77.898m at 31 March 2025 (Under-borrowing, §3.1 page 11). Narrows to £56.249m (25/26 projected), £39.209m (26/27), £27.465m (27/28), £22.877m (28/29). CFR grows £120.942m over the three forward years; external debt (incl OLTL) grows £154.314m — the £169m 3-year borrowing plan closes most, not all, of the internal-borrowing gap.

facts.value: £169m 3-year borrowing requirement to support the 10-year Capital Investment Strategy agreed 26 February 2026. Named drivers: new Dumfries High School, Roads Investment, Dumfries Zero Waste Park, Whitesands Flood Protection Scheme and Stranraer Marina — the last two increased on 11 December 2025 to unlock £75m of external funding. Strategy §4.16: relatively short-term (1–5y) borrowing to be utilised first because MUFG anticipates rates falling over the next two years; some 10y+ needed for refinancing-risk cover.
facts.note: §4.17 explicitly warns that annual borrowing repayments will be closer to the treasury limits in the under 12m, 12m–2y and 2–5y buckets than previously.

facts.value: Excluding OLTL: 5.0% (2024/25 actual), 5.3% (25/26), 5.3% (26/27), 5.8% (27/28), 6.5% (28/29). Including OLTL: 1.7%, 5.8%, 5.6%, 6.0%, 6.7% across the same years. Excluding-OLTL trajectory adds 1.5 percentage points over 4 years — driven by the £169m borrowing plan on top of a scheduled amortisation of £13.7m–£15.9m per year.
facts.note: The 2024/25 Including-OLTL figure (1.7%) sits very low against the following four years (5.6%–6.7%) — likely a one-off IFRS 16 accounting effect in the year it was adopted (see §2.2 page 8 on the 2024/25 £10.6m Service Concession IFRS 16 adjustment).

summary.text:
Dumfries and Galloway's Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27, heard at Full Council on 26 March 2026. The covering report (doc 75253) carries no figures; every treasury number sits in the 32-page appendix (doc 75254) dated February 2026 — both are on disk and both were read. Chief Financial Officer Paul Garrett approved the report. The strategy is set explicitly against MUFG Corporate Markets' 22 December 2025 interest-rate view.

The paper describes an ambitious borrowing plan. £169m over the next three years (§4.14 of the covering report), driven by the new Dumfries High School, Roads Investment, Dumfries Zero Waste Park, and — as of a Full Council decision on 11 December 2025 — an increased contribution to the Whitesands Flood Protection Scheme and Stranraer Marina to unlock £75m of external funding. The Capital Financing Requirement moves from £441.110m at 31 March 2025 actual to £557.802m by 31 March 2029 — up £116.7m. Under-borrowing narrows from £56.249m (25/26 projected) to £22.877m (28/29), i.e. new debt closes most but not all of the internal-borrowing gap. Ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream (excluding OLTL) rises from 5.3% to 6.5% over the same window.

The strategy is very fixed and very long: 100% fixed rate (limit 70–100%), 23.1-year average duration to maturity, 65.22% of debt in the 10-year-plus bucket against a 50% floor. Section 4.20: 'all current borrowing is at a fixed interest rate'. Sections 4.16 and 4.17 announce a deliberate shift into the front end — short-term (1–5y) borrowing to be utilised first because MUFG anticipates rates falling, with the strategy explicitly warning that repayments will run closer to the under-12m, 12m–2y and 2–5y ceilings than previously. The 2-5y bucket sits at 16.44% of a 25% limit today — 8.56 percentage points of headroom.

The paper's arithmetic ties cleanly. The balance-sheet identity CFR − external borrowing − OLTL = internal borrowing checks EXACTLY for 2024/25 actual and to £2k rounding for all four forward projections. The 27 February 2026 portfolio splits 205.988 + 15.000 + 7.051 + 1.324 = 229.363, and 229.363 − 10.027 investments = 219.336 net treasury borrowing — both printed and both tie. No red flags in the paper's own numbers.

The loan-book reconciliation does not tie as cleanly. Our file today holds 61 PWLB loans totalling £210,985,592 at a weighted 4.5888%. Of those, 34 were live on 27 February 2026, totalling £127.7m — 62% of the paper's £205.988m PWLB at that date. Roughly £78m of the loans that were on the book on 27 February 2026 have been repaid or matured before today, and roughly £83m of new PWLB has been drawn since. Consistent with the paper's active-borrower narrative but the reconciliation is not a tie-to-the-pound open. The paper prints no weighted average PWLB rate anywhere, so our 4.5888% cannot be checked against theirs. Disclosed in the draft as our own coverage gap; not solicited as a correction.

The strongest, most falsifiable observation in the paper is the dated rate forecast. Against the 22.12.25 PWLB certainty rates the paper quotes (§3.3 page 13), today's DMO certainty curve is 44–53bp HIGHER at every tenor: 5y 4.81% → 5.34% (+53bp), 10y 5.39% → 5.83% (+44bp), 25y 6.01% → 6.46% (+45bp), 50y 5.78% → 6.27% (+49bp). Bank Rate is 3.75% today; MUFG's 22.12.25 view had Bank Rate at 3.50% by June 2026 and 3.25% by December 2026. The strategy leans deliberately into the short end on the strength of a rates-falling view — eight months on, the market has moved the other way at every quoted maturity. This is the hook.

Draft written. State: needs an address. The paper names Paul Garrett (Chief Financial Officer / Section 95 Officer) as approving, Karen Donaldson as Treasury and Capital Manager, and finance officers Emilia Kopanicka and Megan Widdowson. None of them are published with an email address — the paper gives only a general contact number (030 33 33 3000). Send-by 2026-09-18 as a general batch date; no specific committee date is published for the mid-year report.

officer.body:
Hi [OFFICER NAME],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and the training relevant, we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the strategy you took to Full Council on 26 March. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Your strategy and appendix are unusually clean, and this is offered in that spirit.

One cross-check first, and then a disclosure. The balance-sheet identity in your Section 3.1 ties exactly: £441.110m of CFR less £220.116m of external borrowing less £143.096m of OLTL gives the £77.898m Under-borrowing you print for 31 March 2025. Every forward year ties to two thousand pounds of rounding. On the loan book, our file today carries 61 PWLB loans at a balance of £210.985m against your 27 February 2026 PWLB of £205.988m — but restricted to loans that were live on your reference date, we hold only 34 of them, £127.7m, or 62%. So a fair amount of the book you show on 27 February has come off in the six months since, and a similar amount of new PWLB has been drawn — consistent with the £169m three-year plan in your paragraph 4.14. You publish no weighted PWLB rate to reconcile our 4.5888% against, so that piece we can't test either way. Flagging our own coverage gap rather than glossing it.

The reason we wrote is your Section 3.3, and specifically the four PWLB certainty rates you print as at 22 December 2025 — 5-year 4.81%, 10-year 5.39%, 25-year 6.01%, 50-year 5.78%. Your strategy in 4.16 leans into short-dated borrowing precisely because MUFG expects those to fall, with a two-year-forward target of 4.10%, 4.70%, 5.30% and 5.10% for the same tenors.

Against the DMO's certainty curve this afternoon (notice 314/26, 14 August), those four rates are 5.34%, 5.83%, 6.46% and 6.27% — 44 to 53 basis points higher, not lower, at every one. Bank Rate is 3.75%; the 22 December view had it at 3.50% by June and 3.25% by December. Eight months in, the market has moved the other way at every maturity you quote.

This is not a critique of MUFG's view — forecasts miss, that is what forecasts do, and yours is straightforwardly what you were given by your adviser at the time. It matters because your strategy is 100% fixed, 23.1 years average duration, and 65% of the book beyond ten years — a portfolio built for exactly one direction of travel. Layering in new short-dated PWLB against a rates-falling view, as 4.16 sets out to do, sits well when the view is holding and less well when it isn't. Section 4.17 already notes the treasury indicator headroom on the front-end buckets will be tighter than previously: your 2-5-year bucket sits at 16.44% of a 25% ceiling — 8.6 percentage points of room.

What we publish that speaks to this is not another forecast. It is the market's own implied path — the SONIA/OIS curve — updated daily, plus the DMO's certainty and repayment curves at both fixings.
